passages.claim: A genuine nonzero common orthogonal vector to two prescribed vectors in a three-dimensional normal space is constructed by finite-dimensional orthogonal complement algebra, even for dependent constraints.

The actual nonnegative generated cone is determined by feasible polar directions annihilating two distinct generator rays. A direction with one zero is split into two feasible directions gaining a zero; a direction with no zero is split once first. Exact finite clipping retains every original inequality, and bipolarity supplies actual cone membership. Finite incident conormals then give the complete halfspace presentation from genuine pair-zero ray coverage.

Two tangent endpoint rays and a third independent generator determine the actual conormal line. The exact Riesz-coordinate representation proves feasible directions are nonnegative multiples of the feasible unit conormal, unit conormals are unique, and nonnegative third-generator sign is automatically strict for a unit vector. A three-generator basis is constructed internally in the convenience endpoint.

The literal finite sum of ordinary endpoint arccos angles times actual inward conormals equals twice the actual spherical vector integral, with norm at most twice actual area, for arbitrary finite edge count. All halfspace completeness, support-face wedge identities, actual angular identifications and nonparallelism are proved internally. Native geometric coverage is needed only for nonzero supporting-pair directions; zero requires no artificial incidence.

proof_adaptations: The analytic arbitrary-m balance was already proved by Gaussian hard-threshold integration and exact radial polar integration. This packet proves the missing finite geometric reduction rather than introducing an assumed manifold divergence formula.

Supporting-pair completeness uses two finite line splittings instead of triangulation or a general extremal-ray decomposition. The line clipping is explicitly proved in the separately frozen nonsimple-face polar-line module.

A real linear functional nonnegative on all feasible pair-zero directions is nonnegative on the full polar cone; the final balance does not assume this testing assertion, but derives it from actual finite incident-ray coverage and bipolarity.

The final Coverage endpoints retain actual finite generator/facet incidence, an actual strict polar vector and actual geometric ray coverage. They are intermediate native polygon theorems; they do not yet assert the complete nonsimple Green identity for an original polyhedron.

Spherical area is the actual Euclidean-volume-induced angular measure and facet angular masses are computed from ordinary endpoint arccos angles. No identification with raw unnormalized Mathlib Hausdorff measure is silently claimed.

No previously frozen sources, Root, Audit, detailed correspondence ledgers or global acceptance counts were changed. The prior passed proof commit and existing continuity/Fatou route retain their original scopes.
